typography.instructions: Use JetBrains Mono for all numeric values, scanner readouts, and primary titles to give a terminal/HUD feel. Use Outfit for readable descriptions in the info cards.

layout_and_spacing.spacing_scale: Generous on container edges (p-6, p-8), tight on HUD elements (p-1, p-2)
layout_and_spacing.container_rules: This is a camera-first app. The main view must be h-screen w-screen with the camera background (using a background image if actual camera isn't accessible). UI elements must float above it.
layout_and_spacing.bento_grid: For the scan history, use Mode A: The Tetris Grid (asymmetrical bento layouts) to make it look like a high-tech database rather than a standard list.

component_guidelines.general: Do not use generic SaaS cards. All surfaces must be 'Crystal Glass' or 'Terminal Retro' with sharp inner contrasts.
component_guidelines.camera_viewfinder: Full-screen absolute positioning. Overlay a subtle SVG scanning reticle in the center. Add corner brackets `[ ]` that pulse.
component_guidelines.ar_labels: Absolute positioned small pills floating over the background. Use JetBrains Mono, highly visible neon border (`border-[#00E5FF]`), and background blur.
component_guidelines.info_bottom_sheet: When an object is scanned, a bottom sheet (customized Shadcn Drawer or Dialog mapped to bottom) slides up. It must have crystal glassmorphism (`backdrop-blur-2xl bg-black/70`) with a 1px `border-white/10` top edge.
component_guidelines.buttons: Primary CTA should be the 'Scan' button - a large circular floating action button (FAB) at the bottom center. Needs an outer glowing ring (`shadow-[0_0_15px_rgba(0,255,102,0.5)]`).
component_guidelines.icons: Use Phosphor Icons (React) for a technical, duotone look. e.g. crosshairs, scan, history, corners.

motion_and_interaction.scanning_state: When scanning, animate a horizontal green line moving top to bottom over the view. Use framer-motion.
motion_and_interaction.hud_bootup: On app load, stagger the entrance of the HUD corner brackets and labels (opacity 0 to 1).
motion_and_interaction.data_reveal: Text in the AR labels should ideally use a 'scramble' or typewriter effect on appear.

camera_background_mock.description: Blurred modern living room to simulate the camera feed background.

scanned_plant.description: Example object to place in the center of the camera view for mock scanning (Plant).

scanned_camera.description: Example object to place in the center of the camera view for mock scanning (Vintage Camera).

accessibility_and_testing.contrast: Ensure pure white text has text-shadow when overlaid directly on the camera feed.

instructions_to_main_agent: Build this as a mobile-first web app (h-screen, max-w-md mx-auto for desktop, full width for mobile) simulating a native AR app.
Use standard React .js or .jsx files as per the environment. Do not use TypeScript.
Set the background of the main container to the `camera_background_mock` image with `bg-cover bg-center` to simulate the live camera feed.
Use Framer Motion for the scanning reticle and bottom sheet animations.
Use Phosphor icons or lucide-react for technical iconography.
Do not use generic Shadcn cards for the main UI. Build custom crystal glass panels using the utility classes provided in the colors section.
The UI should feel like a fighter jet HUD mixed with a sleek modern app. High contrast, neon accents, and mono fonts for data.
Ensure the scanning flow feels immersive, with AR labels positioned absolutely over the mock camera background.
